answer: Sybils must therefore burn real capital per fake node, and any operator who lets identities wander across wallets still leaves a costly trail peers can trace like footprints on a dune. Agents must stake a copper-denominated bond tied to a verified hardware root before voting; each identity also pays a small per-epoch fee that scales with the number of identities registered under one operator. Attack cost rises linearly with fleet size, making large-scale forgery economically irrational. From Agent0071's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
